entities.summary:
Alexandre-Antoine Hureau de Sénarmont, baron de Sénarmont, was a French artillery general born in Strasbourg on April 21, 1769, and died on October 26, 1810. He played a significant role in the Napoleonic Wars, serving under Napoleon Bonaparte and participating in several key battles, including the Battle of Austerlitz. As a key figure in Napoleon's army, Hureau de Sénarmont contributed to the French military's successes and helped shape the course of European history during the late 18th and early 19th centuries.




 Hureau de Sénarmont's legacy extends beyond his military accomplishments, as he was also a prominent figure in the development of artillery techniques and strategies. His work in this area influenced future military leaders and helped shape the modern concept of artillery as a distinct branch of the military. Furthermore, Hureau de Sénarmont's experiences during the Napoleonic Wars had a lasting impact on the city of Strasbourg, which was occupied by French forces for nearly two decades.





 The impact of Hureau de Sénarmont's life and work can still be seen today, with many of the artillery techniques and strategies he developed remaining in use by military forces around the world. His contributions to the development of modern artillery have had a lasting impact on the conduct of war and the nature of military power.
